name: val-town
title: Val Town
description: Browse your vals, read their logs and traces, and turn them into tools for Raycast AI
author: KevinBatdorf

commands.name: search-vals
commands.title: Search Vals
commands.subtitle: Val Town
commands.description: Browse your vals, their files, logs, traces, history, SQLite and blobs.

commands.name: manage-tools
commands.title: Manage Tools
commands.subtitle: Val Town
commands.description: Review the vals you tagged as tools and the specs Raycast AI calls them with.

commands.name: errors
commands.title: Errors
commands.subtitle: Val Town
commands.description: Watch chosen val files and notify when a new execution fails.

tools.name: list-tools
tools.title: List Val Town Tools
tools.description: List the tools the user has published from their Val Town account, with the input schema each one takes. Call this first whenever the user asks to run, trigger, or use one of their own vals, tools, scripts, or automations — it is the only way to learn which ones exist and what arguments they accept.

tools.name: execute-tool
tools.title: Execute Val Town Tool
tools.description: Run one of the user's Val Town tools and return its output. The tool name and its arguments must come from list-tools first; do not guess a name. Use this to actually do the thing the user asked for, rather than describing how.

tools.name: get-val-info
tools.title: Get Val Town Val Info
tools.description: Read the files and source code of one val in the user's Val Town account. Use this only when the source itself matters — debugging a failing tool, explaining what a val does, or answering a question list-tools cannot. It is not needed to run a tool.

tools.name: load-skill
tools.title: Load Val Town Skill
tools.description: Load one of the user's own Val Town skills: a written guide that says which of their vals to call and in what order. Call this when the user names a skill or asks for a multi-step routine of theirs, then follow the returned instructions using execute-tool.

ai.instructions: The user keeps callable tools in their Val Town account. Start with list-tools to see what exists and what arguments each takes, then execute-tool to run one. Never invent a tool name or an argument the schema does not list. When the user names a skill, load-skill first and follow its instructions, calling execute-tool for each val it names.

preferences.name: apiToken
preferences.title: Val Town API Token
preferences.description: Create one at val.town/settings/api. Needs read access, plus write if you want to tag vals as tools from Raycast.
